title: "Mail and Storage Operations"
execute:
  eval: false

## Transaction boundary

Submitting a request commits the request and its mail-outbox records in one
SQLite transaction. SMTP is performed later by a separate worker. This means a
mail outage cannot discard an otherwise valid request, and a saved request is
never displayed as a successful ticket until the delivery record says so.

The mail worker runs every minute through `ppsv-mail-outbox.timer`. Start an
immediate run with:

```bash
sudo systemctl start ppsv-mail-outbox.service
sudo journalctl -u ppsv-mail-outbox.service -n 100 --no-pager
```

## Mail identities that may be used

There are only two trusted sender identities:

- the provisioned service address in `PPSV_MAIL_FROM`, normally
  `ppsv-service@biochem.mpg.de`; and
- the authenticated LDAP email, but only when the current profile marks it as
  verified and an end-to-end test has authorized `ldap_from` mode.

An editable email in the request form is never an SMTP `From`, `Reply-To`, or
acknowledgement recipient. If LDAP has no verified email, the service identity
sends the ticket without `Reply-To`; acknowledgement is suppressed and the
condition remains visible to staff.

The application does not provide inbound-mail forwarding or a mailbox relay.
Ticket delivery also fails closed until
`PPSV_SERVICE_IDENTITY_AUTHORIZED_ACK=1`. Every enabled ticket mode requires
`PPSV_TICKET_E2E_TEST_ACK=1` after the real requester/auto-reply test; changing
only the mode string cannot enable an unproved sender or suppress the direct
acknowledgement without evidence that the ticket reply is reliable. The request
remains saved and staff see a suppressed configuration-error delivery row.

## Ticket modes

| `PPSV_TICKET_MODE` | Primary ticket | Failure behavior | Acknowledgement behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| `disabled` | No SMTP attempt; a suppressed outbox row is retained | Request remains saved and visibly not delivered | None |
| `service_reply_to` | `From: PPSV_MAIL_FROM`; verified LDAP address in `Reply-To` when available | Fixed-sender ticket follows the normal retry schedule | With `PPSV_DIRECT_ACK=true`, direct acknowledgement is released only after the ticket succeeds |
| `ldap_from` | Verified LDAP address in `From` | LDAP sender is tried once; on failure the durable service-sender fallback is activated immediately | No direct acknowledgement after a successful LDAP-sender ticket; if fixed-sender fallback succeeds, the configured direct acknowledgement may be released |

The acknowledgement includes a ticket-link sentence only if the ticket adapter
returns a real ticket URL. An application request URL is not presented as a
ticket URL.

## Required SMTP and ticket decision test

Use a dedicated real LDAP test account and a non-production test request. Keep
the delivery-log rows and received-message headers as evidence.

### 1. Authorize the service sender

Ask the SMTP administrators to confirm that the configured relay account may
send as `ppsv-service@biochem.mpg.de`. Configure the safe baseline:

```ini
PPSV_TICKET_MODE=service_reply_to
PPSV_MAIL_FROM=ppsv-service@biochem.mpg.de
PPSV_DIRECT_ACK=true
```

Submit once and prove that the ticket recipient receives the message, `From`
is the service identity, and `Reply-To` is exactly the verified LDAP email.
Also prove that an unverified form email does not appear in either header.

### 2. Determine ticket auto-reply behavior

Observe whether the real ticket system sends its requester acknowledgement to
the `Reply-To` address in `service_reply_to` mode.

- If it reliably does so and the content is accepted by PPSV, set
  `PPSV_DIRECT_ACK=false` to prevent a duplicate.
- If it does not, keep `PPSV_DIRECT_ACK=true`; the PPSV acknowledgement is
  released only after successful fixed-sender ticket delivery.

Repeat the test after configuration and prove the requester receives exactly
one acknowledgement.

### 3. Test authenticated LDAP `From`

Only after the relay team says LDAP sender addresses are allowed, set
`PPSV_TICKET_MODE=ldap_from` and submit with the real test account. Prove both:

1. the relay accepts the authenticated LDAP address as `From`; and
2. the ticket system's requester auto-reply reaches that same LDAP address.

If either condition fails, return to `service_reply_to`. Do not compensate by
using editable form email. Also force or simulate LDAP-`From` rejection once to
prove that the service-sender fallback is activated and that the requester
still receives no duplicate acknowledgement.

Record the chosen mode, relay owner, test date, ticket identifier, exact sender
headers, acknowledgement count, and expected retest interval in the handoff
record.

## Delivery retries and status

The fixed-sender ticket and acknowledgement retry at these elapsed offsets:

1. immediately;
2. 5 minutes;
3. 30 minutes;
4. 2 hours;
5. 12 hours; and
6. 24 hours.

Every attempt records its number, UTC timestamp, success flag, and error. Rows
left in `sending` by an interrupted worker are recovered after the lease. After
automatic attempts are exhausted, an administrator may retry a failed row from
the delivery log. A technician may inspect delivery state but cannot invoke the
admin retry action.

If both a primary and fallback send fail, the request remains saved with failed
delivery state. Do not tell the requester a ticket exists until an outbox row is
actually `sent`.

## Storage layout

Files are outside the web root. For request `PPSV000001`, the primary layout is:

```text
/fs/pool/pool-ppsvf-projects/PPSV000001/
├── inputs/
└── results/
```

The application treats this pool as available only when `findmnt` reports the
exact operator-reviewed `PPSV_POOL_EXPECTED_SOURCE`. If the mount disappears
and leaves an ordinary local mount-point directory behind, uploads use the
fallback instead of writing into the underlying system disk. Local-directory
pool use is an explicit test/development override and must remain disabled in
production.

Requesters may add input files to their own non-closed requests. Staff may add
inputs and results. The application preserves the sanitized original filename
as metadata, but stores content under a generated name with size, MIME type,
uploader, location, and SHA-256 checksum.

The configured limit, normally 75 MB, applies cumulatively to active files in a
request. Optional request-submission files are rejected if neither the primary
pool nor fallback is writable; they are never silently discarded. A request
without files can still be saved with storage state `none`.

Path traversal and symbolic links are rejected. Directories use mode `2770`
and files `0660`; setgid and default ACLs preserve access for
`ppsvf-shiny-user` and `b_profa`. Never change these paths to `0777` or `0666`.

## Pool outage and fallback

When the pool is unavailable or unsafe, the application stores new files under:

```text
/srv/ppsv-app-data/uploads_pending_pool/PPSV000001/{inputs,results}
```

The request is visibly flagged with fallback storage state. The fallback is
persistent and included in the nightly backup; it is not a temporary directory
inside a release.

Before reconciliation, verify that the intended pool is mounted and writable
as the service user. Then run:

```bash
sudo systemctl start ppsv-pool-reconcile.service
sudo journalctl -u ppsv-pool-reconcile.service -n 100 --no-pager
```

The reconciliation operation:

1. reads only active database records whose location is `fallback`;
2. validates that each source is inside the fallback root;
3. verifies its recorded SHA-256;
4. copies it to the matching pool request/category directory without following
   symlinks or overwriting a different file;
5. verifies the destination checksum; and
6. updates the database location only after a verified copy.

The fallback source remains as a safety copy. Remove it only through a separate
operator retention decision after the database, fallback backup, destination
checksum, and facility snapshot have all been verified. The application itself
exposes no permanent purge.

## File archive and download

Archiving is soft and admin-only. It records actor and timestamp and hides the
file from the normal manifest; it does not unlink the stored content. A
technician cannot archive or delete a file.

Every download repeats request authorization, validates that the stored path is
inside the configured root, rejects unsafe paths, and verifies the checksum.
The browser never receives a raw server path.
